text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Swiss food giant Nestle's CEO Helmut Maucher said that the group plans to double revenues in China every second year. Maucher also said that the company will invest some $600 million through the year 2000.

- Students in the German-speaking part of Switzerland study on average three to four semesters longer than students in Swiss French-speaking universities, the Federal Office for Education and Science reported.

- U.S. Senator Alfonse A'Amato and the Jewish Wold Congress repeated accusations alleging that Switzerland profited from funds of missing Jews after World War II. Senior banker Hans Vontobel said in an interview that some banks were arrogant towards Jewish heirs.
- Swiss-Swedish technology group ABB reported that it had received a 630 million Swiss franc order from Indian oil company Essar Oil.
- Swiss computer mouse producer Logitech reported a 62 percent rise in net profit to $4.2 million for the second quarter of fiscal 1996/97 compared with the same period last year.
- Members of the upper house of parliament organized a public hearing on measures the government implemented to fight mad cow disease in Switzerland.
